# git-trim

git-trim automatically trims local tracking branches whose upstream branches are merged or removed.

Installation

- Download a prebuilt binary from the Releases page and place it in a directory on your PATH.

GIT-TRIM(1)                                    General Commands Manual                                    GIT-TRIM(1)

NAME
       git-trim - Automatically trims your tracking branches whose upstream branches are merged or stray.

SYNOPSIS
       git-trim [FLAGS] [OPTIONS]

FLAGS
       -h, --help
              Prints help information

       --no-update
              Do not update remotes [config: trim.update]

       --no-confirm
              Do not ask confirm [config: trim.confirm]

       --no-detach
              Do not detach when HEAD is about to be deleted [config: trim.detach]

       --dry-run
              Do not delete branches, show what branches will be deleted

OPTIONS
       -b, --bases=bases
              Comma separated multiple names of branches. All the other branches are compared with the upstream
              branches of those branches. [default: branches that tracks `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/*/HEAD`]
              [config: trim.bases]

              The default value is a branch that tracks `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/*/HEAD`. They might not be
              reflected correctly when the HEAD branch of your remote repository is changed. You can see the changed
              HEAD branch name with `git remote show <remote>` and apply it to your local repository with `git remote
              set-head <remote> --auto`.

       -p, --protected=protected
              Comma separated multiple glob patterns (e.g. `release-*`, `feature/*`) of branches that should never be
              deleted. [config: trim.protected]

       --update-interval=update_interval
              Prevents too frequent updates. Seconds between updates in seconds. 0 to disable. [default: 5] [config:
              trim.updateInterval]

       -d, --delete=delete
              Comma separated values of `<delete range>[:<remote name>]`. Delete range is one of the `merged,
              merged-local, merged-remote, stray, diverged, local, remote`. `:<remote name>` is only necessary to a
              `<delete range>` when the range is applied to remote branches. You can use `*` as `<remote name>` to
              delete a range of branches from all remotes. [default : `merged:origin`] [config: trim.delete]

              `merged` implies `merged-local,merged-remote`.

              `merged-local` will delete merged tracking local branches. `merged-remote:<remote>` will delete merged
              upstream branches from `<remote>`. `stray` will delete tracking local branches, which is not merged,
              but the upstream is gone. `diverged:<remote>` will delete merged tracking local branches, and their
              upstreams from `<remote>` even if the upstreams are not merged and diverged from local ones. `local`
              will delete non-tracking merged local branches. `remote:<remote>` will delete non-upstream merged
              remote tracking branches. Use with caution when you are using other than `merged`. It might lose
              changes, and even nuke repositories.

EXIT STATUS
       0      Successful program execution.

       1      Unsuccessful program execution.

#!/bin/bash

echo a > a; git add a; git commit -qm "init"
cd ..

cd local
# local-ahead: upstream merged, local has extra commit
git checkout -qb local-ahead
echo b > b; git add b; git commit -qm "local-ahead 1"
git push -q -u origin local-ahead
git checkout -q master
git merge -q --no-ff local-ahead -m "merge local-ahead"
git push -q origin master
git checkout -q local-ahead
echo b2 > b2; git add b2; git commit -qm "local-ahead 2 (extra)"
# squash-merged
git checkout -q master
git checkout -qb squashed
echo c > c; git add c; git commit -qm "squashed 1"
echo c2 > c2; git add c2; git commit -qm "squashed 2"
git push -q -u origin squashed
git checkout -q master
git merge --squash -q squashed && git commit -qm "squash merge squashed"
git push -q origin master

echo d > d; git add d; git commit -qm "rebased 1"
git push -q -u origin rebased
git checkout -q master
echo m > m; git add m; git commit -qm "master progress"
git cherry-pick -q rebased
git push -q origin master

# tracking local branch (remote = .)

cd ..

cd local

git push -q -u origin squashed

git push -q origin master

git push -q -u origin rebased

/// Asks a yes/no question on the terminal (stderr) like `Confirm? [y/N]` and returns the answer.
/// The default answer is `false`.
pub fn confirm(prompt: &str) -> Result<bool, ConfirmError> {
    let mut term = io::stderr();
    if !is_terminal(term.as_raw_fd()) {
        return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotConnected, "not a terminal").into());
    }

    write!(term, "{} [y/N] ", prompt)?;
    // hide cursor
    write!(term, "\x1b[?25l")?;
    term.flush()?;

    let answer = {
        let stdin = io::stdin();
        let mut tty_file: Option<File> = None;
        let fd = if is_terminal(stdin.as_raw_fd()) {
            stdin.as_raw_fd()
        } else {
            let file = File::open("/dev/tty")?;
            let fd = file.as_raw_fd();
            tty_file = Some(file);
            fd
        };
        let mut input: Box<dyn Read> = match tty_file {
            Some(file) => Box::new(file),
            None => Box::new(stdin),
        };
        let _raw = RawMode::enable(fd)?;
        let answer = loop {
            match read_key(&mut *input) {
                Ok(Key::Char('y')) | Ok(Key::Char('Y')) => break Ok(true),
                Ok(Key::Char('n')) | Ok(Key::Char('N')) => break Ok(false),
                Ok(Key::Enter) => break Ok(false),
                Ok(Key::Interrupt) => {
                    break Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted, "interrupted"));
                }
                Ok(_) => continue,
                Err(err) => break Err(err),
            }
        };
        answer
    };
    let answer = match answer {
        Ok(answer) => answer,
        Err(err) if err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => {
            // the user hit ^C: signal SIGINT to ourselves like a normal terminal would do
            unsafe {
                libc::raise(libc::SIGINT);
            }
            return Err(err.into());
        }
        Err(err) => {
            let _ = write!(term, "\x1b[?25h");
            let _ = term.flush();
            return Err(err.into());
        }
    };

    // clear the line and report the selection
    write!(term, "\r\x1b[2K")?;
    writeln!(term, "{} {}", prompt, if answer { "yes" } else { "no" })?;
</output>

The implementation is complete and committed. Summary of the work:

**Approach**
- Explored the binary purely through its CLI: `--help`/`-h`/`-V`, exit codes, and especially `RUST_LOG=trace` output (its normal logging interface), which revealed the processing pipeline (config → optional `git remote update --prune` with background `git ls-remote --symref` checks → base resolution → branch categorisation → `MergeTracker` → parallel classification → worktree/HEAD checks → summary → confirm → `git push --delete` / `git branch --delete --force`).
- Built many scenario repositories (merged, squash‑merged, rebased, stray, diverged, direct‑fetch/URL upstreams, non‑tracking, non‑upstream, multiple remotes/bases, worktrees, detached/unborn HEAD, bare repos, unrelated histories, broken configs) plus a randomized fuzzer, and compared stdout/stderr/exit codes and resulting repository state (including interactive pty sessions) between the original and my build.

**Implementation (Rust, `src/`)**
- `args.rs`: clap builder CLI matching the original help text/errors; `DeleteRange`/`DeleteFilter`/`Scope` parsing with identical error messages.
- `config.rs`: `Explicit`/`GitConfig`/`Implicit` config resolution from `git config trim.*`, default base detection from `refs/remotes/*/HEAD`.
- `branch.rs`: local/remote-tracking/remote-branch types, upstream resolution via refspecs (tracking, direct‑fetch URL, incomplete configs, errors).
- `merge_tracker.rs`: merged-commit cache, `git rev-list --cherry-pick` rebase detection and squash‑merge test commits (`git-trim <git-trim@squash.merge.test.local>`), including the unrelated‑history quirk.
- `core.rs`: classification requests/results, delete-range filtering, keep reasons.
- `main.rs`: orchestration, summary rendering (`*1/*2/*3` hints, `[base]`, `[merged, but: …]`), deletions, HEAD detaching, remote-HEAD out‑of‑sync warning.
- `confirm.rs` (dialoguer‑compatible terminal prompt), `subprocess.rs`, `wildmatch.rs` (fnmatch-style protected patterns), `remote_head_change_checker.rs`.

`compile.sh` builds with cargo (offline first, online fallback) and copies the binary to `./executable`; build artifacts are git-ignored.
